nodes.description: Seizure control was achieved with valproate, carbamazepine or lamotrigine in about 40% of patients with known outcome, while about half had refractory epilepsy. Valproate controlled seizures in an individual case.

evidence.reference_title: [CNKSR2 gene variants causing Houge type of X-linked syndromic intellectual developmental disorder: Seven cases and literature review].
evidence.snippet: Among 34 patients with known epilepsy outcomes, 14 (41.2%) achieved seizure control with valproate, carbamazepine, or lamotrigine; 16 (47.1%) had refractory epilepsy; and 4 (11.8%) were untreated, had unclear seizure status, or were still undergoing treatment adjustment.

evidence.reference_title: CNKSR2 gene mutation leads to Houge type of X-linked syndromic mental retardation: A case report and review of literature.
evidence.snippet: On administration of valproic acid, he had no further seizures.

meta.association: CNKSR2 (Xp22.12) is the only gene associated with this disorder. Pathogenic alleles are almost all predicted loss-of-function: whole or partial gene deletions, nonsense, frameshift and canonical splice variants, with a minority of missense variants.

evidence.reference_title: Absent CNKSR2 causes seizures and intellectual, attention, and language deficits.
evidence.snippet: We detail the disease caused by absence of the synaptic protein CNKSR2 in 8 patients ranging from 6 to 62 years old.

evidence.reference_title: CNKSR2-related neurodevelopmental and epilepsy disorder: a cohort of 13 new families and literature review indicating a predominance of loss of function pathogenic variants.
evidence.snippet: Virtually all of the pathogenic variants are predicted to be loss of function, including genomic deletions, nonsense variants, splice site mutations, and small insertions or deletions.

evidence.reference_title: Novel Digital Anomalies, Hippocampal Atrophy, and Mutations Expand the Genotypic and Phenotypic Spectra of CNKSR2 in the Houge Type of X-Linked Syndromic Intellectual Development Disorder (MRXSHG).
evidence.snippet: Genetic analyses revealed 14 distinct variants in CNKSR2, comprising five nonsense, three frameshift, two splice, and four missense variants, of which 13 are novel.

evidence.reference_title: Loss-of-Function CNKSR2 Mutation Is a Likely Cause of Non-Syndromic X-Linked Intellectual Disability.
evidence.snippet: The maternally inherited deletion removed the initial 15 of the 21 exons of the connector enhancer of KSR-2 gene called CNKSR2 or CNK2.

nodes.description: Germline deletion, truncating, splice or missense variants abolish or destabilize CNKSR2, a multidomain scaffold (SAM, CRIC, PDZ and PH domains and a C-terminal PDZ-binding motif) that binds PSD-95 and S-SCAM at the postsynaptic density and interacts with RAF1, ARHGAP39 (Vilse) and CYTH2. In males the single X carries the variant, so no wild-type copy remains.

evidence.reference_title: Functions of CNKSR2 and Its Association with Neurodevelopmental Disorders.
evidence.snippet: CNKSR2 interacts with different molecules, including RAF1, ARHGAP39, and CYTH2, and regulates the Mitogen-Activated Protein Kinase (MAPK) cascade and small GTPase signaling.

evidence.reference_title: MAGUIN, a novel neuronal membrane-associated guanylate kinase-interacting protein.
evidence.snippet: MAGUIN-1 is localized at the plasma membrane via the plekstrin homology domain and the C-terminal region and interacts with PSD-95/SAP90 and S-SCAM via a C-terminal PDZ domain-binding motif.

evidence.snippet: Virtually all of the pathogenic variants are predicted to be loss of function, including genomic deletions, nonsense variants, splice site mutations, and small insertions or deletions.

genetic_context.description: Hemizygous in affected males; heterozygous in affected females.

nodes.description: Male Cnksr2 knockout mice have increased neural activity, spontaneous electrographic seizures, anxiety, impaired learning and memory, and a progressive loss of ultrasonic vocalizations.

evidence.snippet: Six of 13 males (46.1%) had EEG documenting electrical status epilepticus during sleep, also known as continuous spikes and waves during sleep (ESES/CSWS, families 2, 6, 8, 10, 11, 13).

evidence.reference_title: Expanding the clinical and EEG spectrum of CNKSR2-related encephalopathy with status epilepticus during slow sleep (ESES).
evidence.snippet: Worsening of epilepsy and of cognitive/behavioral disturbances paralleled by enhancement of non-rapid eye movement (NREM) sleep-related, frontally predominant, EEG epileptic discharges [spike-wave-index (SWI): range 60-96%] was consistent with ESES.

nodes.description: CNKSR2 is enriched in dendrites and is needed for normal dendritic spine formation in hippocampal neurons.

evidence.reference_title: Novel Digital Anomalies, Hippocampal Atrophy, and Mutations Expand the Genotypic and Phenotypic Spectra of CNKSR2 in the Houge Type of X-Linked Syndromic Intellectual Development Disorder (MRXSHG).
evidence.snippet: Predominantly expressed in dendrites, CNKSR2 is vital for dendritic spine morphogenesis in hippocampal neurons.

evidence.reference_title: Functions of CNKSR2 and Its Association with Neurodevelopmental Disorders.
evidence.snippet: CNKSR2 has been reported to control the development of dendrite and dendritic spines in primary neurons.

nodes.description: CNKSR2 binds the Rac GTPase-activating protein Vilse (ARHGAP39) and assembles a complex enriched in Rac/Cdc42 regulators (PIX, GIT, PAK, cytohesins), spatially balancing Rac-GDP and Rac-GTP in spines.

evidence.reference_title: The CNK2 scaffold interacts with vilse and modulates Rac cycling during spine morphogenesis in hippocampal neurons.
evidence.snippet: Here, we report that the major binding partner of CNK2 is Vilse/ARHGAP39 and that CNK2 complexes are enriched for proteins involved in Rac/Cdc42 signaling, including Rac1 itself, α-PIX and β-PIX, GIT1 and GIT2, PAK3 and PAK4, and members of the cytohesin family.

nodes.description: In a severely affected girl with CSWS and regression, ethosuximide with sulthiame improved her symptoms. Single case only.

evidence.snippet: Her clinical symptoms were more severe than those of previously reported female patients, but they improved with ethosuximide and sulthiame treatment.

nodes.description: CNKSR2 forms a complex with the ARF exchange factor CYTH2, which protects CNKSR2 from proteasomal degradation; knockdown of either leaves dentate granule cells immature and mispositioned at the boundary of the granule cell layer and hilus in mouse.

evidence.reference_title: The synaptic scaffolding protein CNKSR2 interacts with CYTH2 to mediate hippocampal granule cell development.
evidence.snippet: We found that such manipulations resulted in the abnormal localization of transduced cells at the boundary between the granule cell layer and the hilus.

evidence.reference_title: The synaptic scaffolding protein CNKSR2 interacts with CYTH2 to mediate hippocampal granule cell development.
evidence.snippet: Notably, we show that CYTH2 binding prevents proteasomal degradation of CNKSR2.

nodes.description: Without CNKSR2, PSD-95 is mislocalized and AMPA receptors fail to accumulate at the postsynaptic surface of hippocampal neurons; CNKSR2 normally binds s-afadin and supports this PSD-95-dependent localization.

nodes.description: Increased neural activity with spontaneous electrographic seizures in the Cnksr2 knockout mouse, accompanied by broad changes in the synaptic proteome including epilepsy-associated proteins.

evidence.reference_title: Cnksr2 Loss in Mice Leads to Increased Neural Activity and Behavioral Phenotypes of Epilepsy-Aphasia Syndrome.
evidence.snippet: Proteomics analysis reveals Cnksr2 anchors key binding partners at synapses, and its loss results in significant alterations of the synaptic proteome, including proteins implicated in epilepsy disorders.

nodes.description: CNKSR2-deficient hippocampal neurons respond less to glutamate while presynaptic release is preserved. How this weakening of excitatory transmission relates to the network hyperexcitability seen in vivo is not known.

evidence.reference_title: s-Afadin binds to MAGUIN/Cnksr2 and regulates the localization of the AMPA receptor and glutamatergic synaptic response in hippocampal neurons.
evidence.snippet: Our electrophysiological analysis revealed that the postsynaptic response to glutamate, but not its release from the presynapse, was impaired in the MAGUIN-deficient cultured hippocampal neurons.

nodes.description: Epilepsy starts in early childhood, sometimes before age 5 years. It is often intractable at first, becomes easier to control later in childhood, and in almost all patients resolves by the pre-teen years.

evidence.reference_title: CNKSR2-related neurodevelopmental and epilepsy disorder: a cohort of 13 new families and literature review indicating a predominance of loss of function pathogenic variants.
evidence.snippet: An under-recognized aspect of the epilepsy appears to be that it decreases in severity during childhood and, in almost all instances, resolves in the pre-teen years; knowing this natural history may be useful in guiding seizure management.

evidence.snippet: To conclude, CNKSR2 related D/EE SWAS may be early onset and occur before the age of 5 years in some.

nodes.description: Recurrent nonsense variant reported in an X-linked family with epilepsy-aphasia spectrum phenotypes and, de novo, in a severely affected female. The family report gives the cDNA position as c.2314C>T and the later report as c.2134C>T; codon 712 corresponds to c.2134.

evidence.reference_title: Frequency of CNKSR2 mutation in the X-linked epilepsy-aphasia spectrum.
evidence.snippet: We detected a novel nonsense mutation (c.2314 C>T; p.Arg712*) in one Ashkenazi Jewish family, the male proband of which had a severe epileptic encephalopathy with continuous spike-waves in sleep (ECSWS).

nodes.description: Recurrent nonsense variant from a CGA>TGA transition at a CpG dinucleotide, found de novo in two unrelated males.

evidence.reference_title: Novel splice-site and recurrent p.Arg729* CNKSR2 variants in ESES/CSWS: insights into sex-dependent expression.
evidence.snippet: Our case represents its second independent occurrence, a CGA>TGA transition at a CpG dinucleotide consistent with a mutational hotspot.
